subject.title: an incremental Swift build after adding an enum case reports impossible test failures
subject.text: Adding a 14th case to `Scenario` made `make test` fail with 31 issues, two of which cannot be true of the source: `Expectation failed: (… → .live) == (.live → .fixture(…cleanupSkills))` in ShellClientFactoryTests and TriageSourceGuardTests, both asserting a Release-posture guard that returns .live unconditionally. `git stash` of the two changed source files → 19 tests pass; unstash → the same failures return, which reads as a real regression. It is not. `Choice.live` is encoded in the spare inhabitants of `Scenario`'s tag, so a new Scenario case shifts that encoding, and stale MCPRouterUI object files compiled against the old layout compare a value that no longer means what they think. `rm -rf app/.build` then rebuild: 5/5 pass, then 1512/1512. The hazard for this campaign is the mirror case — a stale build can as easily produce a green — so any test evidence taken across an enum change is taken from a clean build. MITIGATED 2026-08-20: `app/Scripts/enum-layout-stamp.py` hashes the ordered case list of every enum in the package (212 of them) and removes `app/.build` when that hash moves; `make test` now depends on it. The stamp is the case lists rather than the source, so it holds still for an ordinary edit and for a `switch` over the enum — the false positive a naive grep for `^\s*case` would hit — and moves for an added or renamed case. Armed on all four: comment SAME, switch statement SAME, added Scenario case MOVED, renamed Scenario case MOVED, restore back to baseline. The SwiftPM behaviour itself is unchanged and still upstream; what is fixed is this repo's exposure to it.
